chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Zakat upon the slave except the slave acquired for trade, for he is from the wealth upon which Zakat is paid.
ai.seo_question: When is Zakat obligatory on a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of pre-modern Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that slaves are treated as commercial inventory (mal) rather than personal use assets, meaning Zakat is levied only when they are acquired specifically for trade. This distinction highlights the classical view of slavery as an economic commodity within the wealth tax system, a nuance that later jurists debated when applying these rulings to modern contexts. The ruling underscores the principle that Zakat obligations are tied to the purpose of acquisition and the potential for profit generation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no Zakāt upon the slaves except the slave acquired seeking the trading with him, for he would be from the wealth which should be purified (Zakāt paid)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Slaves are not subject to Zakat unless they are for business purposes, because they are from assets that are subject to Zakat.”
